newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says uncovers Qatari spy ring, holds two.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says uncovers Qatari spy ring, holds two.

text.p: Bahrain said on Monday it had arrested a man and a woman from neighbouring Qatar on charges of spying, the official Gulf News Agency reported.
A government official quoted by the agency said Bahrain's security forces had arrested the pair and "they confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Qatar".
The official named them as Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri.
The official said they told the judge they were sent to gather information that could "harm Bahrain's state security and passed it to the Qatari intelligence service."
The 28-year-old Baker, who the official described as a Qatari intelligence officer, and his accomplice would be tried in Bahrain.
Fakhri, 33, had also confessed that she was paid by Qatari intelligence for information she passed on, the agency quoted an official source as saying.
The source said Bahrain had arrested a similar group in January 1987 on charges of spying for Qatar.

Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a territorial dispute over a group of barren islands, reefs and sandbanks which are potentially valuable and of strategic importance. They have been controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.

Qatar, a small peninsula on the east coast of Saudi Arabia, has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. The move has angered the island state of Bahrain which insists on a Gulf Arab solution.
Qatar has said it would only withdraw the case if mediation by Saudi Arabia, the region's dominant power, was successful.
Qatar and Bahrain are members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), an economic and political alliance which also groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates.
Bahrain said it would boycott the GCC's annual summit due to begin in the Qatari capital Doha on Saturday, saying Qatar had behaved in an "unfriendly" manner.
"Bahrain will not take part in meetings being held in Qatar because of unfriendly attitudes Qatar is taking against Bahrain," Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa said last week.
Bahrain in October accused Qatar for the first time of directly backing dissident Shi'ite Moslems in Bahrain seeking political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
